title: Projection right tensor action at rational coefficients
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, an integer $n\ge1$, and an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ containing $E$. Let $S$ be a six-functor datum at these coefficients [def-sf-datum], with the specified operation and comparison data [def-fix-six-functor-datum].

Work at $\Lambda=E$ in the raw rationalized integral categories $D^b_c(T,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi].

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes and supply a compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to Y)$ with $j$ open, $p$ proper and $pj=f$. Write $F=Rf_!^c$, $U=Lf^*$, and $P(K,L)=\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}^c:FK\otimes L\to F(K\otimes UL)$ for the datum's actual compactification projection, namely the proper counit projection followed by the open tensor comparison [def-sf-constructible-projection-mates, def-exchange-projection]. Write $a_T(A,B,C):(A\otimes B)\otimes C\xrightarrow{\sim}A\otimes(B\otimes C)$ for the canonical tensor associator conjugated by the datum's tensor normalization, and $\mu_f(L,N):U(L\otimes N)\xrightarrow{\sim}UL\otimes UN$ for the canonical normalized tensor-pullback comparison [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison]. Then, for every $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $L,N\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, with no additional finite-Tor restriction on these inputs,
$$\begin{aligned}
P(K\otimes UL,N)\circ(P(K,L)\otimes1_N)
={}&F\bigl(a_X(K,UL,UN)^{-1}\bigr)\circ F(1_K\otimes\mu_f(L,N))\\
&\circ P(K,L\otimes N)\circ a_Y(FK,L,N).
\end{aligned}$$
Both sides are morphisms $(FK\otimes L)\otimes N\to F((K\otimes UL)\otimes UN)$. The two final images under $F$ are separate composites. All tensors, associators and pullbacks are the specified completed integral, rationalized, or common-stage operations, according to the coefficient stage. This is an equality of projection maps without an extra invertibility hypothesis. Taking $N$ to be the degree-zero constant quotient $(\Lambda/J)_Y$ for an ideal $J\subseteq\Lambda$ gives reduction inside the original coefficient category; $UN$ is its canonical pulled-back coefficient object. The assertion is for arbitrary $N$, not only constant quotients.

For coefficients, [prop-sf-pf-reduction] supplies the finite reduction square on the finite-Tor domains. At field stages use the integral representatives, rationalization and common-stage comparisons of [thm-sf-pf-field]. The (A5) comparisons [def-sf-datum] and primitive-map data [def-exchange-projection] satisfy the intertwining and cocycle hypotheses of [lem-sf-pf-coefficient-realization-transport]. It carries the proved equal composites and their unit identifications to the specified coefficient/site maps; its cocycles give coefficient naturality. Integral commutativity was proved directly in step 2; fields use chosen integral representatives, never reduction of field objects. For the finite all-ideal clause, [def-sf-constructible-projection-mates] gives the actual component and its recorded source and target realization comparisons. Conjugate by these comparisons and cancel the inverse/hom composites; the fully faithful preimage equation for the realization equivalence identifies the arrow with fixedComponent. Its tensor-coordinate evaluation is the same canonical proper/open projection. Apply the expanded general coefficient-category compactification tensor-action identity [lem-sf-projection-tensor-coordinate-action], proved from the existing generic library calculation in [lem-pur-finite-projection-action-laws] with third input the degree-zero constant quotient A/J. Functorial preservation of composition separates the pullback tensor comparison and the inverse target associator. The quotient is arbitrary; no perfectness or flatness assumption is imposed. The remaining coefficient clauses retain the preceding plan.

proof.text: Write $Q_T:D^b_c(T,R)\to D^b_c(T,E)$ for raw rationalization. By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] it has the same objects: choose the integral objects $K_0,L_0,N_0$ underlying $K,L,N$. Use the same $f$ and the supplied compactification $c$. Apply [lem-sf-projection-reduction-integral] to these three objects. Its hypotheses are exactly the present geometric and coefficient hypotheses; in particular it imposes no finite-Tor condition on $L_0$ or $N_0$. Denote its two composite arrows by $u_0,v_0$. Thus $u_0=v_0$, as arrows from $(F_0K_0\otimes_R L_0)\otimes_R N_0$ to $F_0((K_0\otimes_R U_0L_0)\otimes_R U_0N_0)$.

proof.text: Identify the localized expressions with the specified rational expressions, retaining all endpoint comparisons. [def-sf-operation-stages] says that the rationalization operation comparisons are identities on the specified integral object models. [lem-sf-rational-projection-tensor-compatibility] supplies the tensor comparison and the local square $b_t Q_Y(P_0(A,B))=P_E(Q_XA,Q_YB)b_s$ for each compact-support component. Use it at $(K_0,L_0)$, $(K_0\otimes_R U_0L_0,N_0)$ and $(K_0,L_0\otimes_R N_0)$. [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison] defines the rational $\mu_f$ to be the localization of the integral hom and inverse. The raw-localization part of [lem-pur-bilinear-comparison-coefficient-descent] extends the linear tensor functors and their natural isomorphisms by $h\mapsto h\otimes1$ and preserves composition and whiskering, including the supplied associativity maps. Apply this pointwise at $E$ to the canonical completed tensor and its associator. These operations are the linear extensions prescribed in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; only this raw-localization assertion is used, not the common-field construction. Consequently the canonical rational associator and inverse are the images of the integral ones. For the datum's tensor normalizations, conjugate by its specified tensor equalities on both sides, exactly as in the statement. Equality substitution identifies these conjugated associators; it introduces no monoidal-coherence hypothesis on a freely chosen tensor comparison.

proof.text: Apply the functor $Q_Y$ to $u_0=v_0$. For consecutive arrows $h:A\to B$, $k:B\to C$, the endpoint equations $b_BQ(h)=h_Eb_A$ and $b_CQ(k)=k_Eb_B$ give $b_CQ(kh)=k_Eb_BQ(h)=k_Eh_Eb_A$. Repeat this substitution for the factors of $u_0$ and $v_0$, using Step 2, including tensoring $P_0(K_0,L_0)$ with $1_{N_0}$ and applying compact support to each of the two final arrows. The middle comparisons cancel. Hence, with the same invertible endpoint maps $b_s,b_t$, the two desired rational composites satisfy $u_Eb_s=b_tQ_Y(u_0)=b_tQ_Y(v_0)=v_Eb_s$. Cancel $b_s$ to obtain $u_E=v_E$. Functoriality leaves $F(a_X^{-1})$ and $F(1\otimes\mu_f)$ as the two separate images in the asserted order. This argument uses equality preservation, not faithfulness of rationalization or invertibility of a projection.

proof.text: Every rational object has the integral underlying object used in Step 1, so the equation holds for every $K,L,N$ in the statement. There is no requirement to lift arbitrary rational morphisms: the assertion is a component equation at objects. For an ideal $J\subset E$, substitute the degree-zero constant quotient for $N$. Since $E$ is a field, $J=0$ or $J=E$, giving respectively the coefficient unit or zero object, both permitted inputs. The equation therefore includes both reductions, and its $UN$ is the specified pullback of that input. The proof for general $N$ was already established and has used no flatness, finite-Tor, or projection-invertibility hypothesis.
